claims.text: Vapor deposition can produce a thin, uniform copper coating over all tungsten particle surfaces before consolidation.
Pre-coating tungsten particles with copper before consolidation will yield a void-free W–Cu composite.
Pre-coating tungsten particles with copper will produce uniform bonding between W and Cu.
The vapor-coated W–Cu composite will have better thermal transport than composites made by conventional powder-metallurgical routes.
The vapor-coated W–Cu composite will maintain mechanical durability relative to conventional powder-metallurgical composites.
A continuous, conformal copper coating on each tungsten particle ensures near-perfect interconstituent contact during consolidation.
The deposited copper layer reduces interfacial void formation during sintering.
The deposited copper layer impedes W–Cu phase separation during sintering.
Reduced void formation and more uniform phase distribution create enhanced thermal-conduction pathways.
The coating-mediated structure preserves the composite's mechanical integrity under irradiation stress.
Vapor-coated samples will have a significantly lower void or defect fraction than samples produced by spark-plasma sintering or mechanical alloying without complete pre-coating.
Vapor-coated samples will have higher thermal conductivity than the named conventional baseline.
Vapor-coated samples will retain or improve mechanical durability under fusion-reactor service conditions relative to the conventional baseline.
An inert or reducing processing atmosphere prevents oxidation during coating and consolidation.
A processing window below tungsten's melting point can still provide sufficient temperature for diffusion bonding.
The proposed approach is applicable to fusion-reactor joints exposed to high thermal flux and radiation.

contradictions.description: The central hypothesis requires mechanical durability to be maintained, and the predicted outcome allows it to be retained or enhanced, but the falsification rule requires an increase in mechanical durability. Thus, unchanged durability would satisfy the main hypothesis yet be treated as falsifying it.
